Software Developer
Interview E perience
BHAVESH UPADHYAY l B.Tech Electrical 2020 - 2024
FOR FTE 2024
17th August 2023
BNY Mellon came to our campus to recruit final-year students for an FTE
position as a software developer. There were more than 150 applicants.
Eligibility: 7.5 CGPA Criteria
Branches Allowed: CS, IT, ExTC, Electronics, Electrical, and Mechanical.
Round 1 - Online Assessment (10th August 2023)
Online Test conducted on Hackerrank Platform having 4 DSA Questions to be
completed within 120 Minutes.
1. Count User Logins - In the initial read, I came to the conclusion that this
question is pretty straightforward but the implementation would require
some time, and also solving some edge cases will eat up my time, hence I
decided to leave this question and thought, I would solve it later but I
couldn’t find time later, to reiterate on this question.
2. Binary Storage -
You’re given a binary 2D array of size NxM, each row of the matrix had
some value x denoting the xth bit of the current number is set. Consider
arr[] = {3,2,1} meaning the number would be 1110 which is equivalent to
14, similarly, other N rows would contribute some value you have to sort
in descending order of values and return the indices according to row
number.

Eg - bitArrays = [[0,2],[2,3],[2,1]]
index
binary
decimal
0
0101
5
1
1100
12
2
0110
6
here, the values in order of descending are [12,6,5] so, we return [1,2,0].
I was able to solve this completely.
3. Valid Keys - Can’t recall the question, but I was able to solve this
completely.
4. Team Formation - Given a list of employees, where each is assigned a
numeric score, and there are certain rules for finding the sum of scores
of selected employees.
Rules -
1. The employee with the highest score among the first k employees or
the last k employees in the score list is selected.
2. Selected Employee is removed from the score list.
3. The process continues until team_size is achieved.
Example -
score[] = [10, 20, 10, 15, 5, 30, 20]
team_size = 2
k = 3
Initially, we select first k i.e [10, 20, 10] or last k [5, 30, 20] so, 30 is
selected and removed from the list.
Second time, we have first k i.e [10,20,10] or last k [15,5,20] we take 20
and remove it.
Thus our team reaches a size of team_size so we stop and return 30 + 20
= 50.
I was able to solve this completely using the priority queue.

19 students were shortlisted for the interviews, but later on, 6 more were
shortlisted. All the interviews were conducted in person.
Technical Round 1 (45 mins)
1. The interviewer was very friendly and he made me comfortable by
shaking hands and asking me to get comfortable and also asked If I need
coffee or tea or water, I politely said I’m fine, and we can start the
interview.
2. He went through my resume and asked the very famous “Tell me about
yourself ?”
3. Then he asked whether I know C/C++. I answered C++.
4. He asked me to explain the principles of OOPS, and I asked a clarifying
question whether the question means Pillars of OOPS.
(PS. I explained all the pillars along with real-life examples, it took me around 15 mins to
explain in layman's terms)
5. Difference between Encapsulation and Abstraction?
6. Difference between Early Binding and Late Binding?
(PS. Here I was asked to write code on paper explaining the difference between them)
7. What is class and an object? Explain the difference between them.
8. What is a Transaction?
After this, the interviewer moved on to DSA.
9. He asked me whether I know Data Structures and Algorithms. I said yes.
10. Gave an example of an unsorted array and asked me to list down all the
sorting algorithms on the paper which can be used to sort the given array.

(PS: I only included those that I felt comfortable with)
11. Explain Merge Sort and dry run the algorithm on the array.
After answering this question, I was feeling much more confident.
12. What is the name of the algorithm you were using in the Merge Sort and
why the Time Complexity is O(nlogn)?
(PS. This was asked because I said the algorithm is recursive, I tried to figure it out, but
suddenly he gave me a hint saying what did Britishers do in India, for the time complexity
I pondered on (low+high)/2 he said you’re very close and at the end, I explained to him
why it’s nlogn)
13. Is Merge Sort an in-place algorithm?
14. Lastly, the interviewer asked If I had any questions.
(PS. Always ask 1-2 questions that show that you’re interested in the company as well as
you get to know about the company and the work they do and their tech stack)
6 students were eliminated after this round.

Technical Round 2 (45 mins)
1. This round too started with the famous “Tell me about yourself?”
2. What is Virtual DOM in React?
(PS. Asked because ReactJS was mentioned on my resume)
After this, he moved on to some DSA Questions.
3. What is an array?
4. Given an array find the first repetitive element in it. I first gave the brute
force solution and then he asked me to optimize it which I did by using a
hashmap and immediately wrote the code for both approaches on paper
and tested the code on two test cases. The question was easy but he was
expecting me to write clean and understandable code like using better
naming for variables and data structures. The interviewer looked satisfied
with my solution.
(PS. I asked clarifying questions on this, like will there be cases when there is no repetitive
element, would you like to provide some test cases, is array sorted)
Now, came the twist in the interview, as the interviewer moved on to HR
questions.
5. As I see, you’re from Electrical, then Why Software Engineering?
6. What is the driving force behind putting so much effort into your passion
apart from academics?
(PS. This was a follow-up question from my previous question’s answer)
7. Then he started a general discussion asking did I apply for Deutsche
Bank, Oracle’s on-campus processes, I answered honestly then he asked
how do you handle failures and criticism.
8. Why do you want to join BNY Mellon?
9. Lastly, the interviewer asked If I had any questions.

The interviews were happening parallelly so those who cleared the previous round,
got the mail for the final round.
Hiring Manager Round (15 mins)
1. The interviewer was very friendly and he made me comfortable by asking
questions like how was your day, how are you feeling, and how much you
enjoyed the process.
2. Tell me one good and one bad thing about the interview process today?
3. Again the most famous question, “Tell me about yourself?”
4. Why Software Engineering being from Electrical Background?
5. Why did you choose Electrical Engineering at VJTI, instead of taking
Computer Science in other colleges in Mumbai, I answered by saying VJTI
was my dream college hence I preferred VJTI over a branch.
(PS. The key here is not to criticize anything, but to focus more on your positives)
6. Will you be still working and learning rigorously once you get this
opportunity to work as a Software Developer at BNY Mellon?
7. What is the driving force that kept you motivated while preparing?
8. Why BNY Mellon?
(PS. Always be prepared for these types of questions, and try to make your answer such
that it matches companies core values)
9. Lastly, the interviewer asked If I had any questions.
On that same day, at 9:55 PM, the results were released. 12 students
were chosen, and I was one of them😊.

Tips:
1. Make sure you enter with a smile and greet them because your first
impression can have a lot of impact.
2. Maintain a grooming standard in the interviews, because it impacts your body
language.
3. Stay calm, composed, and confident while speaking.
4. Prepare the “Tell me about yourself” and a few common HR questions
beforehand.
5. For a DSA Question, try to think out loud and share your ideas with the
interviewer.
6. If you finished writing your code, make sure to dry-run it before presenting it
to the interviewer.
7. Try to maintain a smile on your face throughout the interview, that reflects
how much confidence you have.
8. Don’t lose hope in rejection. Your rejections are just a redirection.
Resources (That I followed)
●DSA: Striver’s SDE Sheet, CodeHelp DSA Course, takeUForward
●OOPS: OOPS Roadmap - Love Babbar, OOPS Interviewbit FAQs
●DBMS: DBMS Roadmap - Love Babbar, CodeHelp DBMS Playlist
●OS: OS Roadmap - Love Babbar, OS Interviewbit FAQs
●SQL: CodeHelp SQL One Shot, W3Schools SQL Exercises
●Aptitude: Indiabix, PrepInsta
●Puzzles: GFG Puzzles
“Believe in your preparation and hard work, Results will follow!”
ALL THE BEST👍
PS. For any help, feel free to reach out to me here.
